• Gulnora's barrel holds 50 liters.
• In April, Nodir's barrel filled up 2 times.
• In April, Gulnora's barrel filled up 6 times.
• Both use the water for their vegetable gardens.

The student wants to compare the total amount of rainwater the two neighbours collected in April.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

Nodir's barrel holds 200 liters of rainwater, four times as much as Gulnora's 50-liter barrel.

why.ru: Итоги: у Нодира 2 × 200 = 400 литров, у Гульноры 6 × 50 = 300, то есть у Нодира на 100 больше. Сколько раз наполнялись бочки и их объём — не итог.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Two kinds of wheat were tested on the school farm plot.
• The Oltin wheat was sown in March; the Kumush wheat was sown in April.
• Oltin plants grew 90 centimeters tall.
• Kumush plants grew 60 centimeters tall.
• Both kinds were watered in the same way.
• Each kind gave 4 kilograms of grain per plot.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity in the results of the two kinds of wheat.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: The Oltin and Kumush wheat each gave 4 kilograms of grain per plot.
The Oltin and Kumush wheat plants were watered in the same way on the school farm plot.
Oltin plants grew 90 centimeters tall, 30 centimeters taller than the Kumush plants.
The Oltin wheat was sown in March, a month before the Kumush wheat.

why.en: The results are what each kind gave: 4 kilograms of grain each. The watering is a shared method, not a result, and the heights differ.
why.uz: Natija — har bir navning bergan hosili: har biri 4 kilogrammdan don. Sugʻorish — umumiy usul, natija emas, boʻylari esa farq qiladi.
why.ru: Результат — то, что дал каждый сорт: по 4 кг зерна. Полив — общий способ, а не результат, а высота растений различается.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Jamshid and Madina, two pupils in Grade 11, had summer jobs.
• Jamshid worked at a car wash for 6 weeks, 5 days a week.
• Madina worked at a bookshop for 4 weeks, 6 days a week.
• Each of them earned 2,400,000 som.
• Jamshid worked outdoors; Madina worked indoors.

The student wants to emphasize a difference in the number of weeks the two pupils worked.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Jamshid worked at the car wash for 6 weeks, two weeks longer than Madina worked at the bookshop.
Madina worked at the bookshop 6 days a week, one day more each week than Jamshid worked at the car wash.
Jamshid and Madina each earned 2,400,000 som from their summer jobs.
Jamshid worked outdoors at a car wash, whereas Madina worked indoors at a bookshop.

why.en: The goal is weeks: Jamshid's 6 against Madina's 4, two weeks longer. Days a week and indoor or outdoor work are other differences.
why.uz: Maqsad — haftalar soni: Jamshidning 6 haftasi va Madinaning 4 haftasi, ikki hafta koʻp. Haftadagi kunlar va ish joyi — boshqa farqlar.
why.ru: Цель — число недель: 6 у Жамшида против 4 у Мадины, на две недели дольше. Дни в неделю и работа в помещении — другие различия.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In May, the school moved its bicycle racks from the back yard to the front gate.
• The racks hold 40 bicycles.
• Delivery trucks drive into the back yard every morning.
• The trucks often scratched the bicycles parked there.

The student wants to explain why the school moved the bicycle racks.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: The school moved the racks because the delivery trucks in the back yard often scratched the bicycles.
In May, the school's bicycle racks, which hold 40 bicycles, were moved from the back yard to the front gate.
Every morning, delivery trucks drive into the back yard of the school, where the bicycle racks used to be.
The bicycle racks at the front gate of the school have room for 40 bicycles.

why.en: "Explain why" asks for the reason: the trucks scratched the bicycles. Saying what was moved, or how many bicycles fit, gives no reason.
why.uz: «Explain why» sababni soʻraydi: yuk mashinalari velosipedlarni tirnagan. Nima koʻchirilgani yoki nechta velosiped sigʻishi sabab emas.
why.ru: «Explain why» требует причины: грузовики царапали велосипеды. Что перенесли или сколько велосипедов помещается — не причина.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Class 4B held a sock drive for a children's home.
• For two weeks, pupils brought socks from home.
• In the end, the class collected 350 pairs of socks.
• A teacher drove the socks to the children's home.

The student wants to present the result of the sock drive.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Class 4B's sock drive collected 350 pairs of socks for a children's home.
For two weeks, the pupils of Class 4B brought socks from home for the sock drive.
Class 4B held a sock drive because the class wanted to help a children's home.
A teacher drove the socks that Class 4B had brought in over to the children's home.

why.en: A result is what the drive achieved in the end: 350 pairs of socks. Bringing socks for two weeks is the method, and helping the home is the aim.
why.uz: Natija — aksiya oxirida erishgan narsa: 350 juft paypoq. Ikki hafta paypoq olib kelish — usul, bolalar uyiga yordam — maqsad.
why.ru: Результат — чего добилась акция в итоге: 350 пар носков. Приносить носки две недели — способ, помощь детскому дому — цель.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A "walking bus" is a group of children who walk to school together with two adults.
• It follows a fixed route and picks up children at set "stops" along the way.
• Our school started a walking bus in September.
• Twelve children use it every morning.
• Parents take turns being the two adults.

The student wants to introduce the walking bus to parents who have never heard of one.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: A walking bus is a group of children who walk to school with two adults, picking up others at set stops on a fixed route.
Our school started its own walking bus in September, and twelve children now use it every single morning on the way to school.
The parents of the children who use the walking bus take turns being the two adults who walk with the group.
Twelve of the children at our school walk to school every morning with the walking bus that started in September.

why.en: To introduce something to readers who do not know it, say what it is: children walking to school with two adults, picking up others at stops.
why.uz: Biror narsani uni bilmaydiganlarga tanishtirish uchun u nima ekanini ayting: ikki katta kishi bilan maktabga piyoda boradigan, bekatlarda boshqalarni oladigan bolalar.
why.ru: Чтобы представить незнакомое, скажите, что это: дети идут в школу с двумя взрослыми и подбирают других на остановках.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Hasan sells ice cream from a cart in the park.
• His cart has no electricity.
• He packs the ice cream tubs in a wooden box lined with felt.
• Each morning, he fills the box with ice mixed with salt.
• The ice cream stays frozen until evening.

The student wants to explain how Hasan keeps his ice cream frozen.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Hasan packs his tubs in a felt-lined wooden box that he fills with salted ice each morning.
Even though his cart in the park has no electricity, Hasan's ice cream stays frozen until evening.
Hasan's ice-cream cart in the park has no electricity, so he cannot use a freezer.
Hasan sells ice cream in tubs from a cart that stands in the park all day.

why.en: "Explain how" asks for the way: tubs in a felt-lined box filled with salted ice. That the ice cream stays frozen is the result, not the way.
why.uz: «Explain how» usulni soʻraydi: idishlar kigiz qoplangan, tuzli muz toʻldirilgan qutida. Muzqaymoq erimasligi — natija, usul emas.
why.ru: «Explain how» требует способа: стаканчики в ящике с войлоком и солёным льдом. То, что мороженое не тает, — результат, а не способ.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Kamron wanted to know which of three balls bounces the highest.
• He dropped each ball from a height of 2 meters onto the concrete yard.
• A friend filmed each bounce next to a measuring tape.
• He dropped each ball five times.
• The tennis ball bounced the highest.

The student wants to describe Kamron's method.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Kamron dropped each ball five times from 2 meters onto concrete while a friend filmed the bounces beside a measuring tape.
Kamron found that, of the three different balls he dropped onto the concrete yard again and again, the tennis ball bounced the highest.
Kamron wanted to find out which of three different balls would bounce the highest when dropped onto concrete.
With the help of a friend, Kamron tested three balls in the concrete yard to see which bounced the highest.

why.en: A method says how the test was done: five drops from 2 meters, filmed beside a tape. The tennis ball is the result, and finding out is the aim.
why.uz: Usul sinov qanday oʻtkazilganini aytadi: 2 metrdan besh marta tashlash, ruletka yonida videoga olish. Tennis toʻpi — natija, bilish — maqsad.
why.ru: Метод — как проводили опыт: пять бросков с 2 метров, съёмка у рулетки. Теннисный мяч — результат, а желание узнать — цель.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Malika tested whether bread stays fresh longer in a paper bag or a plastic bag.
• She put one half of a loaf in each kind of bag.
• She left both bags on the kitchen shelf for 3 days.
• After 3 days, the bread in the plastic bag had grown mold.
• The bread in the paper bag was dry but had no mold.

The student wants to present the result of Malika's test.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: After 3 days, the bread in the plastic bag had grown mold, while the bread in the paper bag was dry but free of mold.
Malika put one half of a loaf in a paper bag and the other half in a plastic bag, then left both bags on a shelf for 3 days.
Malika's test showed that a paper bag is the best way to keep every kind of bread fresh for as long as possible.
Malika wanted to know whether bread stays fresh longer in a paper bag or in a plastic bag on the kitchen shelf.

why.en: The result is what Malika found after 3 days: mold in the plastic bag, dry bread without mold in the paper one. "Every kind of bread" goes beyond the notes.
why.uz: Natija — Malika 3 kundan keyin topgan narsa: plastik xaltada mogʻor, qogʻoz xaltada mogʻorsiz quruq non. «Every kind of bread» qaydlardan oshib ketadi.
why.ru: Результат — что Малика увидела через 3 дня: плесень в пластиковом пакете, сухой хлеб без плесени в бумажном. «Every kind of bread» — больше, чем в заметках.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Lantern Walk takes place in the old town on the first Saturday of November.
• Families make paper lanterns at home.
• At 6 p.m., they walk together from the clock tower to the river.
• A brass band plays along the way.
• Last year, about 800 people took part.

The student wants to give an overview of the Lantern Walk to readers who have never been.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: On the first Saturday of November, families carry homemade lanterns from the old town's clock tower to the river while a band plays.
Last year, about 800 people took part in the Lantern Walk, which goes from the clock tower in the old town all the way down to the river.
During the Lantern Walk, a brass band plays as the families make their way from the clock tower down to the river.
Before the Lantern Walk in the old town, families make their own paper lanterns at home.

why.en: An overview gives the whole event in one sentence: when, who, what they do and where. The crowd size or the band alone is a detail.
why.uz: Umumiy tavsif butun tadbirni bir gapda beradi: qachon, kim, nima qiladi va qayerda. Ishtirokchilar soni yoki orkestr — tafsilot.
why.ru: Обзор даёт всё событие одним предложением: когда, кто, что делают и где. Число участников или оркестр — лишь деталь.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The town library now lends umbrellas at its front desk.
• Readers return the umbrella on their next visit.
• The library started lending umbrellas in October.
• Many readers had been arriving soaked on rainy days.
• Wet coats and bags had left many returned books damp.

The student wants to explain why the library started lending umbrellas.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: The library started lending umbrellas because readers arriving soaked were leaving the returned books damp.
Since October, readers have been able to borrow an umbrella at the front desk of the town library.
Readers who borrow an umbrella from the library's front desk return it on their next visit.
The town library now lends its readers umbrellas as well as books.

why.en: The reason is the damp books: soaked readers were leaving them wet. When the lending began and how umbrellas come back are not reasons.
why.uz: Sabab — nam boʻlib qolgan kitoblar: yomgʻirda jiqqa hoʻl boʻlib kelgan kitobxonlar ularni namlab qoʻygan. Qachon boshlangani va soyabon qanday qaytarilishi sabab emas.
why.ru: Причина — сырые книги: промокшие читатели возвращали их влажными. Когда это началось и как возвращают зонты — не причина.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Sevara makes felt rugs in her yard.
• First, she lays out sheep's wool in thin layers.
• Then she sprinkles the wool with hot soapy water.
• Next, she rolls it up tightly in a reed mat and rolls the mat back and forth for an hour.
• Finally, she rinses the felt and dries it in the sun.

The student wants to describe the steps Sevara follows to make felt.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Sevara lays out thin layers of wool, wets them with hot soapy water, rolls them in a reed mat for an hour, then rinses and dries the felt.
In her yard, Sevara makes felt rugs out of sheep's wool and hot soapy water, which she leaves to dry in the sun.
To make her felt, Sevara rolls the wet wool up tightly in a reed mat and then rolls the mat back and forth on the ground for a whole hour.
Sevara's felt rugs are made of sheep's wool that she lays out in thin layers.

why.en: "Describe the steps" needs all of them in order: lay the wool, wet it, roll it for an hour, rinse and dry. One step alone is not the steps.
why.uz: «Describe the steps» barcha qadamlarni tartib bilan talab qiladi: junni yoyish, hoʻllash, bir soat dumalatish, yuvish va quritish. Bitta qadam yetmaydi.
why.ru: «Describe the steps» требует всех шагов по порядку: разложить шерсть, намочить, катать час, промыть и высушить. Одного шага мало.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The old water tower in the park has been turned into a lookout.
• Visitors climb 120 steps to a glass-walled platform.
• The platform is 32 meters above the ground.
• On clear days, visitors can see the mountains from the top.
• A ticket costs 10,000 som.

The student wants to emphasize how high the lookout platform is.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: The water tower's glass-walled lookout platform stands 32 meters above the ground.
The old water tower in the park is now a lookout, with a glass-walled platform and a view of the mountains.
A ticket to climb the old water tower in the park and visit its lookout costs 10,000 som.
On clear days, visitors to the old water tower's lookout can see the mountains.

why.en: The goal names one detail, the height, so the answer gives it: 32 meters above the ground. A sentence that sums up the whole lookout hides it.
why.uz: Maqsad bitta tafsilotni — balandlikni — soʻraydi, javob uni beradi: yerdan 32 metr. Butun minorani umumlashtiradigan gap uni yashiradi.
why.ru: Цель называет одну деталь — высоту, и ответ её даёт: 32 метра над землёй. Предложение обо всей смотровой площадке её прячет.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A seed library lends seeds instead of books.
• Gardeners borrow seeds in spring and grow the plants.
• In autumn, they return seeds saved from their own harvest.
• The town's seed library opened in the old post office in 2025.
• It holds 140 kinds of vegetable and flower seeds.
• Tomato seeds are borrowed most often.

The student wants to introduce seed libraries to readers who are unfamiliar with them.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: A seed library lends seeds instead of books: gardeners borrow them in spring and return seeds from their own harvest in autumn.
The town's seed library, which opened in the old post office in 2025, now holds 140 kinds of vegetable and flower seeds.
Of the 140 kinds of vegetable and flower seeds held by the town's seed library, tomato seeds are borrowed most often.
Gardeners who borrow from the town's seed library grow their plants from seeds kept in the old post office.

why.en: Readers who do not know seed libraries need to be told what one is and how it works: seeds lent in spring and returned from the harvest.
why.uz: Urugʻ kutubxonasini bilmaydiganlarga u nima ekani va qanday ishlashini aytish kerak: bahorda urugʻ beriladi, hosildan urugʻ qaytariladi.
why.ru: Тем, кто не знает библиотек семян, нужно сказать, что это и как она работает: семена дают весной, а возвращают из урожая.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The town museum keeps old embroidered wall hangings in its textile room.
• Bright light makes the colors of old thread fade.
• In 2025, the museum lowered the lights in the room.
• When the room is closed, each hanging is covered with a cloth.
• Visitors may now borrow a small torch to see the details.

The student wants to explain why the museum lowered the lights in its textile room.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: The museum lowered the lights in its textile room because bright light makes the colors of old thread fade.
Since the museum lowered the lights in its textile room in 2025, visitors may borrow a small torch to see the details.
When the textile room of the town museum is closed, each embroidered wall hanging is covered with a cloth.
The town museum's textile room, where the lights were lowered in 2025, holds old embroidered wall hangings.

why.en: The reason is that bright light fades old thread. The torches follow from the change, and the cloth covers are another step, not the reason.
why.uz: Sabab — yorqin nur eski iplarni rangsizlantiradi. Fonarlar oʻzgarishdan keyin paydo boʻlgan, mato yopish esa boshqa chora, sabab emas.
why.ru: Причина — яркий свет выцвечивает старые нити. Фонарики — следствие перемены, а ткань на ночь — другая мера, не причина.

• In March, the town placed 60 shared bicycles at 12 stations.
• Riders unlock a bicycle with a phone app.
• The first 30 minutes of each ride are free.
• In the first month, the bicycles were used for 4,200 rides.
• Most rides were between the railway station and the university.

The student wants to present how much the shared bicycles were used in their first month.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: In their first month, the town's 60 shared bicycles were used for 4,200 rides.
Most of the rides on the town's shared bicycles in the first month were between the railway station and the university.
In March, the town placed 60 shared bicycles, which riders unlock with a phone app, at 12 stations.
On the town's shared bicycles, which stand at 12 stations, the first 30 minutes of each ride are free.

why.en: How much the bicycles were used is the number of rides: 4,200 in the first month. Where most rides went is a finding, but not the one asked for.
why.uz: Velosipedlardan qancha foydalanilgani — safarlar soni: birinchi oyda 4200 ta. Koʻp safarlar qayerga boʻlgani ham topilma, lekin soʻralgani emas.
why.ru: Насколько пользовались велосипедами — это число поездок: 4200 за первый месяц. Куда ездили чаще — тоже вывод, но не тот, что нужен.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In 2025, pupils dug a "rain garden" behind the school gym.
• It is a shallow dip in the ground planted with reeds and irises.
• Rain from the gym roof runs down a pipe into the dip.
• The plants' roots help the water soak slowly into the soil.
• Before, rain from the roof flooded the path to the canteen.
• The garden is 6 meters long.

The student wants to explain how the rain garden deals with the rain from the gym roof.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Rain from the gym roof runs down a pipe into the garden's shallow dip, where the roots of its plants help it soak slowly into the soil.
Before the pupils dug the rain garden behind the gym in 2025, rain from the roof used to flood the path to the canteen.
The rain garden that pupils dug behind the school gym in 2025 is a shallow dip in the ground, 6 meters long, planted with reeds and irises.
The rain garden that pupils dug behind the gym in 2025 has stopped the path to the canteen from flooding.

why.en: "Explain how" asks for the way it works: roof water goes down a pipe into the dip and the roots help it soak in. The flooded path is the old problem.
why.uz: «Explain how» qanday ishlashini soʻraydi: tom suvi quvur orqali chuqurchaga tushadi, ildizlar uni tuproqqa singdiradi. Suv bosgan yoʻlak — eski muammo.
why.ru: «Explain how» требует, как это работает: вода с крыши по трубе идёт в углубление, корни помогают ей впитаться. Залитая дорожка — прежняя проблема.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Paper Boat Race is held every May on the canal in Yangiobod.
• Children fold boats from waterproof paper.
• No boat may be longer than 30 centimeters.
• The boats are set on the water at the old mill and float 200 meters to the bridge.
• The first boat to pass under the bridge wins.
• Last year's winning boat took 4 minutes.

The student wants to introduce the Paper Boat Race to readers who have never seen it.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Every May in Yangiobod, children race paper boats they have folded 200 meters down the canal, from the old mill to the bridge.
Last year's winning boat in the Paper Boat Race took 4 minutes to float the 200 meters from the old mill to the bridge.
No boat that children fold from waterproof paper for the Paper Boat Race may be longer than 30 centimeters.
In the Paper Boat Race on the canal in Yangiobod, the first boat to pass under the bridge is the winner.

why.en: An introduction says what the event is: when, where, who takes part and what happens. The winning time, the size rule or how a boat wins is a detail.
why.uz: Tanishtirish tadbir nima ekanini aytadi: qachon, qayerda, kim qatnashadi va nima boʻladi. Gʻolib vaqti, oʻlcham qoidasi yoki qanday yutish — tafsilot.
why.ru: Представление говорит, что это за событие: когда, где, кто участвует и что происходит. Время победителя, правило размера — лишь детали.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In early spring, farmers in the valley paint the lower trunks of their apricot trees white.
• The paint is made of lime mixed with water and clay.
• On sunny winter days, dark bark warms up fast and then freezes again at night, which can split it.
• White paint reflects the sun and keeps the bark cooler.
• The paint washes off slowly over the summer.

The student wants to explain why the farmers paint the trunks white.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: The farmers paint the trunks white because the paint reflects the sun, so the bark does not warm up and then split in the night frost.
The white paint that the farmers in the valley put on the lower trunks of their apricot trees every spring is made of lime mixed with water and clay.
In early spring, the farmers in the valley paint the lower part of each apricot tree's trunk white.
The white paint on the apricot trees in the valley washes off slowly over the summer months.

why.en: The reason is the bark: white paint reflects the sun, so the bark does not warm up by day and split in the night frost. What the paint is made of is no reason.
why.uz: Sabab — poʻstloq: oq boʻyoq quyoshni qaytaradi, shuning uchun poʻstloq kunduzi qizib ketmaydi va kechasi sovuqda yorilmaydi. Boʻyoq nimadan tayyorlangani sabab emas.
why.ru: Причина — кора: белая краска отражает солнце, и кора не нагревается днём и не трескается ночью. Из чего сделана краска — не причина.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• For four weeks, the school library set aside a "quiet corner" where no talking was allowed.
• Pupils could choose to sit there or at the main tables.
• A librarian counted each day where pupils sat.
• On average, 14 pupils a day chose the quiet corner and 9 chose the main tables.
• The library plans to make the quiet corner larger.

The student wants to present the main finding of the four-week test.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: On average, 14 pupils a day chose the library's quiet corner, more than the 9 who chose the main tables.
The four-week test in the school library showed that pupils prefer to study in silence wherever they are.
For four weeks, a librarian counted each day where the pupils chose to sit in the school library.
After the four-week test, the school library is planning to make its quiet corner larger.

why.en: The finding is what the count showed: 14 pupils a day in the quiet corner against 9 at the main tables. "Wherever they are" goes far beyond the notes.
why.uz: Topilma — sanoq koʻrsatgan narsa: kuniga 14 oʻquvchi sokin burchakda, 9 tasi asosiy stollarda. «Wherever they are» qaydlardan juda oshib ketadi.
why.ru: Вывод — то, что показал подсчёт: 14 учеников в день в тихом уголке против 9 за общими столами. «Wherever they are» — далеко за рамками заметок.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In June, 40 volunteers counted the trees along every street in the town center.
• The center was divided into 20 areas, one for each pair of volunteers.
• Each pair walked the streets of its area and marked every tree on a paper map.
• In all, they counted 3,150 trees.
• The most common tree was the plane tree.

The student wants to describe how the volunteers counted the trees.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Working in pairs, each with one of 20 areas, the volunteers walked their streets and marked every tree on a paper map.
The 40 volunteers counted 3,150 trees in the town center, and the plane tree was the most common kind.
In June, 40 volunteers set out to count the trees along every street in the town center.
The most common of the 3,150 trees that the volunteers counted in the town center was the plane tree.

why.en: "Describe how" asks for the method: pairs, one area each, walking the streets and marking each tree on a map. The total and the commonest tree are results.
why.uz: «Describe how» usulni soʻraydi: juft boʻlib, har biriga bitta hudud, koʻchalarni yurib, har bir daraxtni xaritada belgilash. Jami son va eng koʻp daraxt — natija.
why.ru: «Describe how» требует метода: пары, у каждой свой участок, обход улиц и отметка каждого дерева на карте. Итог и самое частое дерево — результаты.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The old merchant's house in the town center was built around 1880.
• Its mud-brick walls are almost a meter thick.
• Thick mud walls take many hours to warm up in the sun.
• A small pool in the courtyard cools the air that flows into the rooms.
• In July, the rooms stay about 10 degrees cooler than the street.
• The house is now a museum of crafts.

The student wants to explain how the old merchant's house stays cool in summer.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: The house's thick mud-brick walls take hours to warm up, and a pool in the courtyard cools the air that flows into its rooms.
In July, the rooms of the old merchant's house in the town center stay about 10 degrees cooler than the busy street outside.
The old merchant's house, built around 1880 with mud-brick walls almost a meter thick, is now a museum of crafts.
The courtyard of the old merchant's house, which is now a museum of crafts, has a small pool in it.

why.en: "Explain how" asks for the way: slow-warming thick walls and a courtyard pool that cools the air. Being 10 degrees cooler is the result, not the way.
why.uz: «Explain how» usulni soʻraydi: sekin qiziydigan qalin devorlar va havoni sovitadigan hovuz. 10 daraja salqinroq boʻlish — natija, usul emas.
why.ru: «Explain how» требует способа: толстые стены, которые медленно греются, и бассейн, охлаждающий воздух. На 10 градусов прохладнее — результат.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The town's new community choir gave its first concert in March.
• Anyone over 12 may join, and no audition is needed.
• It rehearses on Wednesday evenings in the school hall.
• At the first concert, 112 singers stood on the stage.
• The youngest singer was 12 and the oldest was 84.
• The concert raised money for new curtains for the hall.

The student wants to emphasize how many people sang at the first concert.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: At the community choir's first concert in March, 112 singers stood on the stage.
The community choir, which anyone over 12 may join without an audition, rehearses on Wednesday evenings.
At the community choir's first concert, the youngest singer was 12 and the oldest was 84.
In March, the town's new community choir gave its first concert to raise money for new hall curtains.

why.en: The goal names one fact, how many sang, so the answer gives the number: 112 singers. The ages are another detail, and the rest is an overview.
why.uz: Maqsad bitta faktni — nechta kishi kuylaganini soʻraydi, javob sonni beradi: 112 xonanda. Yoshlar — boshqa tafsilot, qolgani umumiy maʼlumot.
why.ru: Цель называет один факт — сколько человек пели, и ответ даёт число: 112 певцов. Возраст — другая деталь, остальное — обзор.

The bus drivers in our town call the last bus of the night "the owl." ______ it is the bus that leaves the station at midnight and stops wherever a passenger asks.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

why.en: The second sentence explains what the drivers' name "the owl" means, in plain words: a link that explains a term, "That is,".
why.uz: Ikkinchi gap haydovchilar qoʻygan «the owl» nomi nimani anglatishini oddiy soʻzlar bilan tushuntiradi: atamani izohlovchi bogʻlovchi «That is,».
why.ru: Второе предложение простыми словами объясняет, что значит прозвище «the owl»: связка, поясняющая термин, — «That is,».

Lola's little brother likes the new picture book that his aunt gave him. ______ he loves it so much that he sleeps with it under his pillow and asks for it every single night.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

why.en: The second sentence goes further than "likes": he loves it and sleeps with it. A stronger claim takes "In fact,", not "In other words,".
why.uz: Ikkinchi gap «likes» soʻzidan ham uzoqqa boradi: u kitobni juda yaxshi koʻradi va u bilan uxlaydi. Kuchliroq fikr uchun «In fact,», «In other words,» emas.
why.ru: Второе предложение идёт дальше, чем «likes»: он обожает книгу и спит с ней. Более сильное утверждение — «In fact,», а не «In other words,».

why.uz: Umumiy fikr (har xil ehtiyojlar), soʻng uning aniq qismlari (pandus, tutqichlar, lift): tafsilot bogʻlovchisi «Specifically,». Fikr kuchaymaydi.
why.ru: Общая мысль (самые разные потребности), затем её точные части (пандусы, поручни, лифт): связка, которая вводит подробность, — «Specifically,». Ничто не усиливается.

Every grandchild in our family wants one of the cotton quilts that Grandmother sews by hand. ______ the quilts are heavy, and they take two days to dry after washing. Still, they stay warm for decades, unlike the cheap blankets sold at the bazaar.

why.en: The writer admits a weak spot (heavy, slow to dry), then turns back with "Still,": granting, then insisting. The link is "Admittedly,".

why.ru: Автор признаёт слабое место (тяжёлые, долго сохнут), а затем возвращается к своему через «Still,»: уступка. Связка — «Admittedly,».

The new rules for the town's food market are all aimed at cleanliness. ______ every stall must now have a covered bin, meat and fish must be kept on ice, and the whole square is washed down each evening after closing.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

why.en: The general point (rules aimed at cleanliness) is followed by the exact rules: a detail link, "Specifically,". "In fact," would need a stronger claim.
why.uz: Umumiy fikrdan (tozalikka qaratilgan qoidalar) keyin aniq qoidalar keladi: tafsilot bogʻlovchisi «Specifically,». «In fact,» uchun kuchliroq daʼvo kerak edi.
why.ru: За общей мыслью (правила ради чистоты) идут сами правила: связка, которая вводит подробность, — «Specifically,». «In fact,» требовало бы более сильного утверждения.

stem.en:
The oldest bookshop in town has outlived every one of the shops that once competed with it. ______ it has outlived the very street it opened on: the road has been renamed twice and rebuilt once, but the shop has stayed in the same small room since 1952.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

why.en: Outliving even its own street goes further than outliving its rivals: a stronger claim, so "In fact,". It is not the same point said again.
why.uz: Oʻz koʻchasidan ham uzoq yashash raqiblardan uzoq yashashdan ham kuchliroq: bu kuchliroq daʼvo, shuning uchun «In fact,». Bu qayta aytish emas.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Gulbahor dyes wool in her village workshop.
• She uses only plants: onion skins for yellow and walnut shells for brown.
• She dyes about 30 kilograms of wool a month.
• Carpet weavers in the region buy most of her wool.
• She learned the craft from her aunt.

The student wants to state what Gulbahor uses to dye wool and who buys most of it.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Gulbahor dyes wool with plants such as onion skins and walnut shells, and carpet weavers in the region buy most of it.
Gulbahor, who learned the craft of dyeing from her aunt, dyes about 30 kilograms of wool a month in her village workshop.
Gulbahor uses onion skins to dye wool yellow and walnut shells to dye it brown in her village workshop.
Carpet weavers in the region buy most of the wool that is dyed in the village workshops.

why.en: The goal has two halves: what she dyes with (plants) and who buys most of it (carpet weavers). Only one option gives both; the others give one or neither.
why.uz: Maqsad ikki qismli: nima bilan boʻyaydi (oʻsimliklar) va koʻpini kim sotib oladi (gilam toʻquvchilar). Ikkalasini faqat bitta variant beradi.
why.ru: У цели две части: чем она красит (растениями) и кто покупает большую часть (ковровщики). Обе части даёт только один вариант.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A hay box is a wooden box packed tightly with hay.
• A pot of food is brought to the boil on a stove and then shut inside the box.
• The hay keeps the heat in, so the food goes on cooking slowly for hours.
• Zebo's family uses a hay box to cook beans.
• It saves them gas.

The student wants to introduce hay boxes to an audience unfamiliar with them.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: A hay box is a wooden box packed with hay, in which a pot brought to the boil goes on cooking for hours because the hay keeps the heat in.
Zebo's family cooks its beans in a hay box, which saves the family a good deal of the gas it would otherwise use on the stove.
In Zebo's family, a pot of beans is first brought to the boil on the stove and then shut inside a wooden box.
The hay inside the box that Zebo's family uses keeps the heat in for hours.

why.en: Readers who do not know hay boxes must be told what one is and how it works: hay holds the heat, so the boiled pot keeps cooking. Zebo's beans are a detail.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In 2026, the town library changed its opening hours.
• It now opens from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., four hours longer each day than before.
• To pay for the longer days, it now closes on Mondays.
• It holds 12,000 books.
• Most of the new evening visitors are students.

The student wants to emphasize the library's longer opening hours while acknowledging that it now closes on Mondays.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Although it now closes on Mondays, the town library stays open four hours longer on the other days, from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.
Although the town library now stays open four hours longer each day than before, from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., it closes on Mondays.
Most of the new evening visitors to the town library, which holds 12,000 books, are students.
The town library now opens from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., which is four hours longer each day than it used to be.

why.uz: Urgʻu gapning asosiy qismiga tushadi: uzaytirilgan soatlar oʻsha yerda, dushanba yopilishi esa «although» qismida. Bir variant ularni teskari qoʻygan.

• The show is on air at 9 a.m.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Four footbridges cross the canal in the old town.
• The Mill Bridge, built in 1890, is made of brick.
• The Market Bridge, built in 1902, is made of brick.
• The School Bridge, built in 1935, is made of brick.
• The Garden Bridge, built in 1961, is made of brick and has an iron railing.

The student wants to make a general statement about what the canal's footbridges are made of.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: All four footbridges over the canal in the old town are made of brick.
The four footbridges over the canal in the old town were built between 1890 and 1961.
The Mill Bridge, built in 1890, is the oldest of the four brick footbridges over the canal.
The Garden Bridge, the newest footbridge over the canal, has an iron railing.

why.ru: Общее утверждение охватывает все заметки одной мыслью: все четыре моста кирпичные. Годы постройки — тоже общее, но это не материал.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The school canteen replaced its long rows of tables with small round tables for six.
• The head cook hoped that pupils would talk more and rush less.
• Lunch now lasts 25 minutes on average, up from 15.
• The food left on plates has fallen by a third.
• A local carpenter made the tables.

The student wants to explain why the canteen changed its tables and present one result of the change.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: The canteen switched to small round tables so that pupils would talk more and rush less, and lunch now lasts 25 minutes instead of 15.
Since the canteen switched to round tables, lunch has lasted 25 minutes on average, and a third less food is left on the plates.
The head cook replaced the long rows of tables in the school canteen because she hoped that pupils would talk more and rush less at lunch.
The canteen's new round tables, each of which seats six pupils, were made by a local carpenter.

why.en: Two halves: why (to make pupils talk more and rush less) and one result (lunch now lasts 25 minutes). One option gives only the results, another only the reason.
why.uz: Ikki qism: nega (oʻquvchilar koʻproq gaplashib, kamroq shoshilishi uchun) va bitta natija (tushlik endi 25 daqiqa). Bir variantda faqat natija, boshqasida faqat sabab.
why.ru: Две части: зачем (чтобы ученики больше говорили и меньше спешили) и один результат (обед длится 25 минут). В одном варианте лишь итоги, в другом — лишь причина.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The town bought 5 electric buses in 2025.
• They are much quieter than the old diesel buses.
• Each can run 180 kilometers before it needs charging.
• The diesel buses could run 500 kilometers on a full tank.
• Charging takes 4 hours.

The student wants to emphasize how quiet the electric buses are while acknowledging their shorter range.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Although each can run only 180 kilometers before charging, the town's electric buses are much quieter than its old diesel ones.
Although the town's electric buses are much quieter than its old diesel ones, each can run only 180 kilometers before charging.
The old diesel buses could run 500 kilometers on a full tank, far more than the 180 kilometers of the new electric buses.
The 5 electric buses that the town bought in 2025 take 4 hours to charge.

why.en: Quietness is X, the main part; the shorter range is Y, the "although" part. The option that puts the range in the main part stresses the drawback instead.
why.uz: Sokinlik — X, asosiy qism; qisqa masofa — Y, «although» qismi. Masofani asosiy qismga qoʻygan variant aksincha kamchilikni taʼkidlaydi.
why.ru: Тишина — это X, главная часть; малый запас хода — Y, часть с «although». Вариант с запасом хода в главной части подчёркивает недостаток.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A dutar is a long-necked instrument with two strings.
• Its name means "two strings."
• It is played by plucking the strings.
• Zarifa, a music student, has played the dutar since she was eight.
• She will play it at the spring concert.

The student wants to introduce the dutar to an audience unfamiliar with it and say who will play it at the spring concert.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Zarifa, a music student, will play the dutar, a long-necked instrument with two plucked strings, at the spring concert.
Zarifa, a music student who will play at the spring concert, has been playing the dutar ever since she was eight years old.
The dutar, whose name means "two strings," is a long-necked instrument that is played by plucking.
At the spring concert, a music student named Zarifa will play an instrument that she began learning at eight.

why.en: Both halves are needed: what a dutar is, for readers who do not know it, and who will play it. One option names Zarifa without saying what a dutar is.
why.uz: Ikkala qism kerak: dutorni bilmaydiganlar uchun u nima ekani va uni kim chaladi. Bir variant Zarifani aytadi, lekin dutor nima ekanini aytmaydi.
why.ru: Нужны обе части: что такое дутар — для тех, кто не знает, — и кто будет играть. Один вариант называет Зарифу, но не говорит, что такое дутар.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In 2024, a village replaced its street lamps with solar lamps.
• The solar lamps cost 4 times as much to buy as the old lamps.
• They need no electricity from the grid.
• The village's electricity bill for street lighting fell to zero.
• On cloudy winter nights, some of the lamps go dark before midnight.
• Each lamp has a small battery.

The student wants to emphasize the savings from the solar lamps while acknowledging that they sometimes go dark.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Although some of them go dark before midnight on cloudy winter nights, the solar lamps have cut the village's street-lighting bill to zero.
Although the solar lamps have cut the village's street-lighting bill to zero, some of them go dark before midnight on cloudy winter nights.

• Komila wanted to know which cover keeps garden soil damp the longest.
• She covered one bed with straw, one with sawdust, and left one bare.
• She watered all three beds equally on Monday.
• On Friday, she measured how damp the soil was with a meter.
• The straw bed was the dampest; the bare bed was the driest.
• She now covers all of her beds with straw.

The student wants to describe how Komila compared the covers and present what she found.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Komila covered one bed with straw and one with sawdust, left one bare, watered all three equally, and found on Friday that the straw bed was dampest.
Komila covered three garden beds with straw, with sawdust and with nothing at all, and then she watered all three of them equally on Monday.
When Komila measured her three beds on Friday, the one covered with straw was the dampest, and the bare bed was the driest of all.
Komila now covers all of her garden beds with straw to keep the soil damp.

why.en: Two halves: the method (three beds, three covers, equal water) and the finding (the straw bed was dampest). One option stops at the method, one gives only the finding.

why.ru: Две части: метод (три грядки, три покрытия, поровну воды) и вывод (под соломой влажнее всего). Один вариант даёт лишь метод, другой — лишь вывод.

Pear slices brushed with lemon juice stayed unbrowned for 3 hours at room temperature.
Apple slices went brown the fastest, in 10 minutes, twice as fast as the banana slices.

A tuner found that the heaters in the classroom had been drying out the wooden parts of the school's old piano, made in 1968.
The school moved its old piano to an inside wall, well away from the classroom heaters, and put a bowl of water inside its case in winter.

• Each bicycle carries up to 80 kilograms.

The student wants to emphasize the money the family saved while acknowledging that deliveries are slower.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

Although the switch to cargo bicycles saved Mansur's family 6 million som in its first year, a delivery across town now takes 35 minutes instead of 20.

• Hawthorn has sharp thorns.
• The farm planted it because deer were eating the young apple trees.
• The farm's wooden fences had needed repairs every year.
• The hedge is now 2 meters tall.

The student wants to explain what a living fence is to an audience unfamiliar with it and why the Rahimov farm planted one.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: A living fence is a row of shrubs planted close enough to stop animals; the Rahimov farm planted one of hawthorn because deer were eating its young apple trees.
In 2023, the Rahimov farm planted a hawthorn fence around its orchard because deer had been eating the young apple trees growing there.

The Rahimov farm's living fence of hawthorn, planted around the orchard in 2023, is now 2 meters tall.

why.en: Two halves: what a living fence is, for readers who do not know, and why the farm planted one (the deer). One option skips the definition, one skips the reason.

• Hulkar timed how long ice cubes of different sizes took to melt on a plate in her kitchen.
• A 10-gram cube melted in 25 minutes.
• A 20-gram cube melted in 40 minutes.
• A 40-gram cube melted in 65 minutes.
• An 80-gram cube melted in 110 minutes.
• The kitchen was at 22°C.

The student wants to make a general statement about how the size of a cube and its melting time were related.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: In Hulkar's test, the bigger an ice cube was, the longer it took to melt.
In Hulkar's test, doubling the size of an ice cube doubled the time it took to melt.
In Hulkar's test, the 80-gram ice cube took 110 minutes to melt, the longest of the four.
In Hulkar's test, the 40-gram cube melted in 65 minutes, 40 minutes longer than the 10-gram cube.

why.en: The general statement covers all four cubes: bigger cubes took longer. "Doubling" is false (20 grams took 40 minutes, not 50), and the rest are single cubes.
why.uz: Umumiy fikr toʻrttala kubni qamraydi: kattaroq kub uzoqroq eridi. «Doubling» notoʻgʻri (20 gramm 50 emas, 40 daqiqada eridi), qolganlari bitta kub haqida.
why.ru: Общее утверждение охватывает все четыре кубика: чем больше, тем дольше. «Doubling» неверно (20 г таяли 40 минут, а не 50), остальное — об одном кубике.

• Over two years, visitors can see every carpet in the collection.

why.ru: Увидеть всю коллекцию — X, главная часть; маленький зал — Y, часть с «although». Вариант, где они поменяны, подчёркивает тесноту зала.

• Bus drivers complain that the bumps shake their passengers.

The student wants to explain the purpose of the speed bumps and present their effect on the cars' speed.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

To slow down the cars near the primary school, the town put speed bumps on Bog Street in May, at a cost of 20 million som.
Since May, the average speed on Bog Street has fallen from 50 to 30 kilometers an hour, but bus drivers say the bumps shake their passengers.
The speed bumps that the town put on Bog Street in May cost 20 million som, and bus drivers complain about them.
